name: Michaud & Persinger 1985: 5 Hz for 60 s during a 3-min story
origin: Michaud & Persinger 1985 (Laurentian University); fields from commercial 'Relaxit' devices
summary: The lab's earliest narrative-memory test: while you listen to a 3-min story, a 5 Hz field runs at one side of the head for the first 60 s, then stops. Michaud & Persinger (32 students, 4 per cell) reported that people given 5 Hz during minute 1 or 2 later made more inferences about the first minute's material than the 20 Hz and sham groups (about 10 against 6).
notes: 32 students heard a 3-min story (Michaud 1985 p.1 [416]) wearing a helmet with a commercial 'Relaxit' device attached 'on either the left or right side at the level of the temporal lobe'. 24 got a 5 Hz or 20 Hz field for 60 s in minute 1, 2 or 3, 4 per cell, and 8 a sham (p.2 [417]). This program plays the arm with 5 Hz in minute 1, on one coil at T7. The paper used each side for half its subjects, so T7 is one of the two sides used. The waveform is described only in an earlier paper that was not available (Mantle & Persinger 1983): the smooth sine here is an assumption. Field: the paper gives only an upper bound, 1 gauss or less (1000 mG, 100 uT), with no place (p.2 [417]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's field model gives about 24 uT at the scalp and 56 uT at the coil face, which the paper neither confirms nor contradicts. Result: 10.4 inferences with 5 Hz against 6.5 with 20 Hz and 6.1 with sham (p.2 [417]), about 1.6 to 1.7 times, less than the abstract's 'twice'. 4 people per cell, one lab, never tested by another group. You need a recorded 3-min story you have not heard. Afterwards retell it in writing and count the direct recalls and the inferences for each minute of the story. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in a quiet room; start the 3-min story and the program together.
schedule: One exposure per person in the original (between groups). For a self-test, use a new story each time and the app's Blind option, and have the retellings scored by someone who does not know the condition.
source: Michaud & Persinger 1985, Geophysical variables and behavior: XXV. Alterations in memory for a narrative following application of theta frequency electromagnetic fields, Percept Mot Skills 60:416-418 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4000856/ ; Richards, Persinger & Koren 1993, Modification of activation and evaluation properties of narratives by weak complex magnetic field patterns that simulate limbic burst firing, Int J Neurosci 71:71-85 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8407157/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

phases.name: Minute 1 of the story: 5 Hz field (60 s)
Minutes 2-3 of the story: no field
